resolution_source: Final official 2026-27 Premier League table (premierleague.com/tables) after the last matchday (~2027-05)
independence_attestation: No betting odds, prediction-market prices or forecast-aggregator numbers were fetched or consulted during this research pass. Honesty caveat: the engine's config files (which contain market blocks) were read earlier in this session for integration work; the numbers below were built base-rate-first from the cited research sources and no market figure is cited, used, or averaged in.

base_rate_used.reference_class: Two blended references: (a) PL teams starting a season with 7+ straight wins - only Chelsea 2005-06 and Liverpool 2019-20 before now, both won the title (2/2, tiny n); (b) the broader class of early-season leaders after ~7-8 games, roughly half of whom win the title
base_rate_used.source: Premier League historical starts (SI/Opta roundups of best starts); blend of 2/2 perfect-start record with ~0.5 leader-after-8 rate

evidence: Table as of 2026-10-19 (MD7): City 21 pts (7/7 wins, GD +12), Arsenal 18, Brighton 16 (GD +18), Chelsea 13, Liverpool 12; Haaland leads scoring with 8
City's 7/7 is only the third such start in PL history; the prior two both converted to titles
Arsenal are the defending champions (won 2025-26 by 6 points over City) and sit only 3 behind with 31 games left - the chaser is the strongest possible kind

Material tail risk: City are appealing a verdict finding them guilty of 114 charges relating to financial rules (2009-2018). The forecast's own resolution rule says a sanctioned table is the real table, so an in-season points deduction would directly hit this question
questions.strongest_opposing_case: Seven games is 18% of a season; titles are not won in October. Arsenal just beat this City side to the title months ago and trail by one result. City's underlying margin (GD +12 vs Brighton's +18) is good, not dominant. And the 114-charge guilty verdict hangs over the season: even a modest points deduction applied to the 2026-27 table would likely be decisive, and that risk is uniquely City's.
questions.reasoning_summary: Base ~0.55 (perfect-start record 2/2 blended with ~0.5 for leaders after 7-8 games, small-n discounted). Adjust down for the quality of the chaser (defending champions 3 points back) and down again for non-trivial sanction tail risk (~10% chance a deduction materially applies this season). Adjust up modestly for the perfect start and Haaland's form. Net: 0.48.

base_rate_used.reference_class: Defending champions sitting 2nd, ~3 points off the lead after 7-8 games; defending champions retain the PL title roughly a third of the time overall
base_rate_used.source: PL history: 10 of 33 completed PL titles were retained by the holder; position after 7 games only mildly updates this

evidence: Arsenal 18 pts from 7 (6W 1L), 3 behind City, as of 2026-10-19
Arsenal won 2025-26 by 6 points over City - the squad that beat this exact rival is intact and the sample of 7 games contains their only loss
City's sanction tail risk is, symmetrically, Arsenal's single biggest upside scenario
questions.strongest_opposing_case: City have dropped zero points and have the league's best scorer; a 3-point gap to a team converting at 100% compounds quickly, and Arsenal already burned their head-to-head margin for error by losing once. Brighton (+18 GD) could also take points off Arsenal in the chasing pack.
questions.reasoning_summary: Base ~0.30 for a defending champion one result off the lead. Small downgrade for City's perfect start (the gap is deeds, not fixture noise); small upgrade for proven head-to-head superiority last season and the City sanction scenario. Net: 0.30 stands.

base_rate_used.reference_class: Probability the champion comes from the top two after 7-8 games: in most PL seasons the eventual champion is already in the top two at this stage (roughly three-quarters of seasons)
base_rate_used.source: PL history of champion position after ~8 games (Opta/Analyst early-season roundups)

evidence: Sum of the two individual assessments above (0.48 + 0.30 = 0.78) cross-checks the set directly
The nearest outsiders: Brighton 3rd (16 pts, GD +18 but no title pedigree), Chelsea 5 off the pace, Liverpool 9 off after 7 games
questions.strongest_opposing_case: Brighton's +18 goal difference in 7 games is an elite underlying signal and they have no European distraction pedigree pressure; Leicester 2015-16 proved a non-traditional champion can come from this kind of start. Liverpool at 9 back with Isak scoring is not dead across 31 games.
questions.reasoning_summary: Set probability = sum of member assessments, 0.78, consistent with the ~0.75 base rate for the champion already being top-two at this stage. Brighton is the live third candidate and caps this below 0.85. Final: 0.78.

base_rate_used.reference_class: Teams 9 points off the lead after 7 games winning the PL title: very rare - comebacks of 9+ points from this early exist (e.g. Man City 2011-12 trailed by less; Man United 1992-93) but are a few percent of seasons
base_rate_used.source: PL history of deficits overturned from matchday 7-8 positions

evidence: Liverpool 12 pts from 7 (3W 3D 1L), 9 behind a City side converting at 100%
Isak has 5 league goals (2nd in the league) - the attack functions; the draws are the leak
Three teams, not one, stand between Liverpool and the lead (City, Arsenal, Brighton)
questions.strongest_opposing_case: A 9-point gap in October has been closed before; Liverpool's underlying quality (recent champions pedigree, elite scorer) exceeds a 12-from-7 start, and if City take a points deduction the entire chasing pack reprices at once.
questions.reasoning_summary: Base ~0.05 for a 9-point deficit after 7 games, needing to overhaul three teams. Squad quality argues no further discount; the multi-team traffic ahead argues no upgrade. Final: 0.05.

base_rate_used.reference_class: Probability the eventual champion is in the top 5 after 7-8 games: in PL history the champion has almost always been top-5 at this point (Leicester 2015-16 were top-5 after 8; true outside-top-5-at-MD8 champions are exceptional)
base_rate_used.source: PL history of champion position after ~8 games

evidence: The named five (City, Arsenal, Brighton, Chelsea, Liverpool) hold the top 5 as of 2026-10-19; the question resolves against these five clubs as frozen, per resolution rules
Best-placed outsiders: Brentford/Leeds/Everton at 10 pts, 11 behind City - all would need a historic run plus a five-team collapse
Every plausible title contender by squad value and recent history is inside the frozen set except Man United (7 pts, 14 behind)
questions.strongest_opposing_case: The frozen-list rule cuts both ways: if a Newcastle/Man United tier side surges while Chelsea and Liverpool fade, the set loses its insurance members. A City points deduction would also inject chaos benefiting exactly the mid-table chasers outside the five.
questions.reasoning_summary: Base ~0.93 that the champion is already top-5 at MD7-8. The frozen set contains every current plausible contender; outsiders are 11+ points back. Slight discount for 31 games of variance and the sanction-chaos scenario. Final: 0.92.
